proof.text: For any scheme $R$ and maps $a:R\to T_i$ and $b:R\to T_j$ with $q_i\circ a=q_j\circ b$, put $A=a^{-1}(W_i)$. The composite $A\to R\to T_i$ has image in $W_i$, so the defining lifting property of an open subscheme gives a map $f:A\to W_i$ over $T_i$. This uses only the open subscheme construction [def-weil-open-immersion], not the base-change theorem for general open immersions.

proof.text: Evaluate $\alpha_i$ on the $T_i$-object $A\to R\to T_i$ and the map $f$. This gives an element of $F(A\to T)$. The equality of composites to $T$ identifies exactly the two structure morphisms $A\to T$. Apply the inverse of $\alpha_j$ at the $T_j$-object $A\to R\to T_j$ to get a $T_j$-map $g:A\to W_j$. Its triangle identity gives $b(A)\subseteq W_j$, hence $a^{-1}(W_i)\subseteq b^{-1}(W_j)$. Apply this to the two projections of $R=T_i\times_T T_j$ [def-pc-fibre-product], using their defining commutativity relation, and then exchange $i$ and $j$ to get equality of inverse-image opens. No naturality, sheaf condition or compatibility of the isomorphisms is required.

title: Descent of the support of etale-local open representatives
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with all schemes, sets and functors in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $F:(\mathit{Sch}/T)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{Sets}$ be a presheaf, where $\mathit{Sch}/T$ has objects scheme morphisms $Z\to T$ and arrows commuting with these maps. Let $\{q_i:T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ be a set-indexed jointly surjective family of etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism]. For each $i$, let $W_i\subseteq T_i$ be an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] and suppose given a natural isomorphism $\alpha_i:h_{W_i/T_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}F|_{T_i}$ of presheaves on $\mathit{Sch}/T_i$, where $h_{W_i/T_i}(Z)=\operatorname{Mor}_{T_i}(Z,W_i)$ and $F|_{T_i}(Z\to T_i)=F(Z\to T_i\to T)$. Then for every $i,j$ the inverse images of $W_i$ and $W_j$ in $T_i\times_TT_j$ [def-pc-fibre-product] are equal as open subschemes. There exists a unique open subscheme $U\subseteq T$ such that $q_i^{-1}(U)=W_i$ as open subschemes of $T_i$ for every $i$. No sheaf condition on $F$, compatibility hypothesis on the $\alpha_i$, finiteness of $I$, or quasi-compactness of the schemes is assumed.
